newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish ex-premier Reynolds appeals libel ruling.
newsitem.headline: Irish ex-premier Reynolds appeals libel ruling.

text.p: Former Irish prime minister Albert Reynolds said on Friday he would appeal against a British court's decision to award him only one penny in damages for a newspaper article which said he had misled parliament.
A jury in London's High Court decided in November that Reynolds had been libelled by an article in Britain's Sunday Times on the events leading up to the fall of his coalition government.
But the jury said the article had not been malicious and awarded Reynolds no damages. A judge later changed the award to the minimum possible of one penny (two cents).
Reynolds has to pay the bulk of his legal costs as he had rejected a higher settlement offer from the Sunday Times.
Irish newspapers estimate his legal bill to be around 800,000 pounds ($1.3 million).
Reynolds said the judge's final comments at the end of the 24-day case had unfairly influenced the jury.
"The overall summing-up was unbalanced and grossly unfair and that undoubtedly affected the jury's verdict on malice and damages," he told Irish radio.

Reynolds helped create Northern Ireland's best chance of peace in a generation, forging a peace plan with British Prime Minster John Major which led to a 17-month ceasefire by Irish Republican Army guerrillas fighting to unite Northern Ireland with the Irish Republic.
